newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian shipping firm cuts fees to spur exports.
newsitem.headline: Algerian shipping firm cuts fees to spur exports.

text.p: Algeria's main shipping company, Societe Nationale des Transports Maritimes, has cut fees by up to 50 percent for exporters in a drive to increase non-energy exports, Algeria's official news agency APS said on Wednesday.
SNTM, with a fleet of more than 30 ships, serves more than 29 ports in Africa, the United States, Asia and Europe.
The Algerian government, striving to bolster export outside the hydrocarbon sector, aims to quadruple non-oil and gas exports to $2 billion by the year 2000.
Non-oil and gas exports were at $538 million in 1996, up from $350 million in 1995.
Half of Algeria's non-oil and gas exports were with former Soviet Union countries because of long-term deals related to the North African country's foreign debt to these countries.
More than one third of non-hydrocarbon exports went to the European Union, mainly France, official figures showed.
